subject: QBR prep: roadmap health brief & launch exposure register
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: roadmap health brief & launch exposure register

Team —

We need a concise health snapshot for the upcoming QBR (7/6). Focused asks below so leadership can take a single-pane look at launch exposure for the next two sprints. Please reply inline by EOD Thur (6/24) with the requested bullets.

1) Product milestone status (on-track / at-risk) + percent complete. If at-risk, call out the specific blocker.
2) Key engineering risks materially impacting launch timeline (list, impact, ETA to fix).
3) Primary mitigation(s) and owners; any remaining unknowns that need exec attention.

Id like to include any external customer impacts for top accounts (Acme Payments is flagged). If there are attachments (status sheet, logs, short canary plan), drop them in the thread.

Thanks — keep it tight, bullets are perfect.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: roadmap health brief & launch exposure register

Neha — quick update from Product / PM side: 

- New API quota controls (M1) — at-risk, 65% complete. Blocker: dependency on telemetry export contracts with EdgeCloud (export schema mismatch causing test failures). Owner: Marissa Cole. Attachment: milestone-status.xlsx (sheet: M1-summary).
- Model catalog rollout (M2) — on-track, 80% complete. No critical open blockers; still validating multi-region routing. Owner: Priya N. (cc not on thread).
- Canary UX changes (M3) — at-risk, 40% complete. Blocker: engineering needs a stable KV cache fix to avoid state flapping during canary. Owner: Marissa + Irene.

Customer impact: Acme Payments is on a pilot using M1. If telemetry export stalls, their billing reconciliation will be delayed; theyve asked for a firm date. Ive flagged this for the QBR executive chairs.

Marissa
Product Director

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: roadmap health brief & launch exposure register

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We need a concise health snapshot for the upcoming QBR (7/6). Focused asks below ...

Providing engineering details and short mitigation plan: 

- Risk A: KV cache corruption under short-lived canaries. Impact: canary traffic causes churn and OOMs in a subset of GPUs; launch window could slip by 2+ weeks if not contained. ETA fix (dev): 4 business days for a targeted patch, plus 2 days for canary validation. Owner: Irene Choi (eng), Jason (infra). Attachments: kv-cache-bug.log (excerpt).

- Risk B: Telemetry export schema mismatch with EdgeCloud sinks. Impact: failed exports prevent Acme reconciliation; blocks M1 for affected customers. ETA: coordination with EdgeCloud + updated adapter expected in 6 business days. Owner: Marissa (PM) + Samir (EdgeCloud).

Mitigations proposed: 
- Short-term: Disable aggressive KV eviction during canaries; enable read-only cache in canary lanes. Owner: Infra lead (Jason). ETA: 24 hours to config change + immediate monitoring.
- Mid-term: Patch KV delta handling in runtime path (target patch above). Owner: Eng core.
- For telemetry: fast-track an adapter shim at the service edge (temporary translation layer) while we align schemas. Owner: Samir (EdgeCloud) + Redwood eng.

Ive also sketched a minimal canary rollback and isolation plan for the QBR pack — see canary-plan.pdf. If leadership wants, I can include the short tech note in the exec pack.

Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Engineering

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Cole <jenna@acme-payments.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: roadmap health brief & launch exposure register

Thanks for the updates — clear and helpful. Executive guidance below (to be included in the QBR slide pack):

1) Accept short-term mitigation for canary (disable aggressive eviction) immediately. Irene, please run the config change tonight and notify ops. Confirm when done.
2) For telemetry export: Marissa, coordinate with Samir and Samirs team to land the adapter shim within 6 business days. Jenna, we will provide a date and a mitigation path; ask Acme to accept the temporary shim for pilot reconciliation.
3) Ask to leadership: If the KV patch slips beyond 10 business days, we will propose a narrow launch window for non-canary customers and a parallel pilot plan for Acme. I will escalate to the sales execs if needed.

Ill draft a one-slide summary for the QBR highlighting: Key exposures (KV canary, telemetry export), immediate actions taken, owners, and proposed contingency (narrow launch / pilot). Neha, include this in the exec pack.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Operations
Redwood Inference
